summary.LAUNCH: A strong, well-evidenced opportunity with no red flags.

summary.KILL: The evidence says the money is better spent elsewhere.
summary.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: Too little fresh evidence to make a call either way.
summary.BLOCKED: This can't be advertised as it stands, whatever the opportunity.

trigger.POLICY_VIOLATION: The live copy breaks a rule

advice.EXPIRED_OFFER: Extend the offer's end date or stop the campaign. Resuming with an expired offer would advertise something people can't get.
advice.INVALID_DESTINATION: Fix the page the button points to, then resume. Sends to a dead link waste the audience's click.
advice.POLICY_VIOLATION: Edit the copy so it follows the rule, or remove the rule if it no longer applies, then resume.
advice.REVOKED_APPROVAL: Ask a current approver to look at the live round again before resuming.
advice.BRAND_RISK: Read the headlines. If they're about a different brand or story, mark it a false alarm.
advice.MANUAL_STOP: Resume once whatever prompted the stop is sorted out.

circuit.resumedToast: Resumed. Held sends go out on the next pass, after one more check.
circuit.falseAlarmToast: Marked as a false alarm. Held sends go out on the next pass.
circuit.onlyManagers: Only owners and admins can resume a paused campaign.
circuit.publishedNote: Posts that already went out stay up: the breaker stops new sends.
circuit.offerHint: When this passes, the campaign pauses on its own.
circuit.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Our supplier just recalled this batch
circuit.stoppedToast: Stopped. No new sends go out.
circuit.revokedToast: Approval revoked. Sends are on hold.
circuit.cantStop: Owners, admins and approvers can stop sends.

impact.title: Proof of impact
impact.sub: Did this campaign cause extra sign-ups? A randomly chosen group gets nothing, and the difference is the campaign's effect.
impact.emptyBody_one: Run the {{n}} email recipient as a randomized experiment before the first send.
impact.emptyBody_other: Run the {{n}} email recipients as a randomized experiment before the first send.
impact.hypothesisPlaceholder: e.g. Emailing commuters raises qualified sign-ups
impact.plan: {{recipients}} recipients give a smallest group of about {{group}}. To reliably detect a {{effect}}-point lift you need about {{needed}} per group.
impact.planShort: With fewer, expect an inconclusive result unless the effect is large.
impact.planUnknown: Enter an expected rate and a lift to see the sample you need.
impact.controlNote: The control group is picked at random and never emailed. Their sign-ups still count, so the campaign is compared with what would have happened anyway.
impact.abNote: Without a control group this compares variant B with variant A. It can't show whether emailing at all made a difference.
impact.declaredToast: Experiment pre-registered. It starts with the first email.
impact.declaredNote: Starts with the first email; from then on the design can't change.
impact.notAnalyzed: Running. The first analysis appears within the hour.

reason.INTERVAL_ABOVE_ZERO: The whole 95% interval of the lift is above zero.
reason.INTERVAL_BELOW_ZERO: The whole 95% interval of the lift is below zero.
reason.INTERVAL_WITHIN_MIN_EFFECT: The 95% interval sits within ±{{effect}} points: any effect is smaller than the bar set in advance.
reason.INTERVAL_TOO_WIDE: The 95% interval includes both no effect and an effect worth acting on.
reason.INSUFFICIENT_DATA: A group is smaller than the minimum set in advance.
reason.NO_OUTCOME_DATA: No conversions were reported for anyone. Check the conversion integration.
reason.SAMPLE_RATIO_MISMATCH: The groups' sizes don't match the planned split, so the assignment can't be trusted.

impact.interimNote: Interim numbers. The verdict comes at the predeclared end ({{when}}), so nobody stops early on a lucky peek.
impact.relativeThin: Not shown: too few control conversions for a stable baseline
impact.chartCaption: Lift in percentage points with its 95% interval. The shaded band is ±{{effect}} points, the smallest effect worth acting on.
impact.revenueNoEstimate: No estimate (mixed currencies or too little data)
impact.attributionModel: Purchases within {{days}} days of clicking. Some would have happened anyway.
impact.srmOk: Group sizes match the planned split.
impact.srmBad: Group sizes don't match the planned split: the assignment broke.
impact.noConversionsYet: No conversions reported yet. Is the conversion integration set up?
impact.unmatched_one: {{n}} conversion didn't match anyone in the experiment and isn't counted.
impact.unmatched_other: {{n}} conversions didn't match anyone in the experiment and aren't counted.
impact.banditFed: The learning model was updated with these conversions.
impact.banditNotFed: The learning model wasn't updated: the data isn't valid for it.

assumption.INTENTION_TO_TREAT: Everyone counts in the group they were assigned to, whether or not the email arrived or was opened.
assumption.OUTCOME_WINDOW_FIXED: Only conversions between the first send and the end of the {{days}}-day attribution window count.
assumption.CONTROL_SEES_OTHER_CHANNELS: The control group can still see social posts: this measures what the email adds on top.
assumption.CONVERSIONS_MATCHED_BY_TOKEN_OR_EMAIL: Conversions are matched by the link token or the email address. Someone who signs up with another address isn't matched, in either group.
assumption.UNMATCHED_CONVERSIONS_EXCLUDED: Conversions from people outside the experiment are left out.

impact.stopRuleValue: Fixed: {{days}} days of sending plus a {{window}}-day window; at least {{min}} per group; acting on a lift of {{effect}}+ points
impact.integrationBody: Every emailed link carries a ciq_t token. When someone signs up, post it (or their email address) with an API key that has the write scope. Retries with the same event_id count once.

ci.title: Competitors
ci.subtitle: What the competitors you name are doing, seen through public sources you approve, and what you could do about it.
ci.addSub: Name them and, if you like, the page and the market to watch.
ci.name: Name
ci.market: Their market, as people search it (optional)
ci.addNote: The page and a news search are added as sources, but nothing is fetched until you approve them.
ci.addedToast: {{name}} added. Approve its sources to start watching.
ci.permitted: Pages are read at most once a day, only where the site's robots.txt allows it, as an identified visitor. Nothing is crawled beyond what you list.
ci.affectsNone: None of your live campaigns is in this market.

reason.UNCONFIRMED: Only one unconfirmed report so far: wait for a second source or their own channels.
reason.NO_LIVE_CAMPAIGN_AFFECTED: None of your live campaigns competes here.
reason.OFFER_ENDED: Their offer ended: nothing to answer.
reason.DEEP_OFFER_ON_YOUR_MARKET: A deep offer in your market: buyers will weigh it against yours.
reason.AVOID_PRICE_WAR: Matching a modest discount starts a price war; stress what's different instead.
reason.BUYERS_WILL_COMPARE: A new product in your market: buyers will compare.
reason.POSITIONING_MOVED: Their positioning moved: make yours clearly distinct.
reason.THEME_ONLY: A theme, not a move: worth watching.
reason.RESPOND_COSTS: Answering directly costs budget and can look reactive.
reason.MONITOR_WAITS: Watching costs nothing but can be slow.
reason.DIFFERENTIATE_NEEDS_ANGLE: Needs a clear angle of your own.
reason.NO_ACTION_RISK: Doing nothing risks losing buyers who compare.

ci.inferredTitle: Why might they have done it?

hypothesis.DEMAND_SOFTENING: Demand is softening and they want volume.
hypothesis.NEW_AUDIENCE: They're going after a new audience.
hypothesis.CATEGORY_EXPANSION: They're expanding into a new category.
hypothesis.PLANNED_ROADMAP: A planned release on their roadmap.

ci.forecast: Search interest in “{{keyword}}” over the next {{days}} days
ci.unresolvable: Couldn't be checked (no data for that week).
ci.limitsTitle: Some sources couldn't be read: this view may be incomplete.
ci.timelineSub: Observed changes with their source and time. Several reports of one story count once.
ci.noEvents: No moves seen yet. The first fetch of a page is a baseline: changes show from the next one.
ci.approveFirst: Approve a source below to start watching.
ci.recordSub: Each move comes with a forecast of search interest in “{{keyword}}”, checked when its two weeks are up.
ci.modelHeldOut: On {{n}} held-out past forecasts the model was off by {{model}}% on average (no-change guess: {{naive}}%); its {{level}}% range held {{coverage}}% of the time.
ci.ownRecord_one: Here: {{count}} forecast checked, {{inside}} inside its range, off by {{error}}%.
ci.ownRecord_other: Here: {{count}} forecasts checked, {{inside}} inside their range, off by {{error}}% on average.
ci.ownRecordNone: No forecast for this competitor has been checked yet.
ci.noMarket: Add their market's search term to get forecasts.
